scope: Leviticus 16–17, all 50 public verses. Prior revisions remain unchanged.

source.verse_hash_method: SHA-256 of the exact original XML verse substring, including written/read notes, not a normalized substitute.
source.public_versification_note: Public and Hebrew numbering align throughout Leviticus 16–17. The full original XML record at 16:21 includes written hand and read hands forms; no numbering shift occurs in this batch.

delta_method: F0 retained wording; F1 lexical; F2 syntax/idiom; F3 consequential interpretive, textual, social, or versification choice. Editorial assessments are separate from similarity scores. Independent review has not occurred.

verses.rationale: Retains the connection to the sons' deaths and drawing near; does not add strange fire, which this verse does not name.
verses.before: The LORD spoke to Moses after the death of Aaron’s two sons, when they drew near before the LORD and died.
verses.after: The LORD spoke to Moses after Aaron's two sons died when they drew near before the LORD.
verses.tsw_comparator: The LORD spoke to Moses after the death of Aaron’s two sons, when they drew near before the LORD and died.

verses.rationale: Identifies the space behind the curtain as the inner sanctuary and retains atonement cover from Exodus. The restriction is not an absolute ban on entry, and the death warning and divine cloud remain.
verses.before: The LORD said to Moses, “Tell Aaron your brother that he must not enter at any time into the Holy Place inside the curtain, before the atonement cover that is upon the ark, or he will die, for I will appear in the cloud over the atonement cover.
verses.after: The LORD said to Moses, “Tell your brother Aaron that he must not enter the inner sanctuary whenever he wishes, going behind the curtain before the atonement cover on the ark. Otherwise he will die, because I appear in the cloud above the atonement cover.
verses.tsw_comparator: The LORD said to Moses, “Tell Aaron your brother that he must not enter at any time into the Holy Place inside the curtain, before the atonement cover that is upon the ark, or he will die, for I will appear in the cloud over the atonement cover.

verses.rationale: Keeps the permitted approach, bull and ram, and their different offering roles; with does not imply that animals enter the inner room.
verses.before: Aaron will enter the Holy Place in this way: with a young bull for a sin offering and a ram for a burnt offering.
verses.after: This is how Aaron must enter the inner sanctuary: with a young bull for a sin offering and a ram for a burnt offering.
verses.tsw_comparator: Aaron shall enter the Holy Place in this way: with a young bull for a sin offering and a ram for a burnt offering.

verses.rationale: Preserves all four linen garments, their holiness and bathing before dressing; no ornate outer garments are added to this phase.
verses.before: He will put on the holy linen tunic, with linen undergarments next to his body, bind himself with the linen sash, and wrap the linen turban around his head. These are holy garments. He will bathe his body in water and then put them on.
verses.after: He must wear a holy linen tunic and linen undergarments next to his body, tie on a linen sash, and wrap a linen turban around his head. These are holy garments. He must bathe his body in water before putting them on.
verses.tsw_comparator: He shall put on the holy linen tunic, with linen undergarments next to his body, bind himself with the linen sash, and wrap the linen turban around his head. These are holy garments. He shall bathe his body in water and then put them on.

verses.rationale: Retains two male goats jointly designated for the sin offering, the single ram and the community as their source.
verses.before: From the congregation of the Israelites he will take two male goats for a sin offering and one ram for a burnt offering.
verses.after: From the Israelite community he must take two male goats for a sin offering and one ram for a burnt offering.
verses.tsw_comparator: From the congregation of the Israelites he shall take two male goats for a sin offering and one ram for a burnt offering.

verses.rationale: Keeps Aaron's own bull and household atonement in the preliminary overview without changing the repeated instruction in verse 11.
verses.before: Aaron will present the bull of the sin offering that is for himself and make atonement for himself and for his household.
verses.after: Aaron must present the bull for his own sin offering and make atonement for himself and his household.
verses.tsw_comparator: Aaron shall present the bull of the sin offering that is for himself and make atonement for himself and for his household.

verses.rationale: Retains both goats, presentation before the LORD and the tent entrance as their location.
verses.before: Then he will take the two goats and set them before the LORD at the entrance of the Tent of Meeting.
verses.after: He must take the two goats and stand them before the LORD at the entrance to the tent of meeting.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then he shall take the two goats and set them before the LORD at the entrance of the Tent of Meeting.

verses.rationale: Preserves the parallel lots and untranslated Azazel, leaving its debated referent to a note rather than making scapegoat or a demon name certain.
verses.before: Aaron will cast lots over the two goats, one lot for the LORD and one lot for Azazel.
verses.after: Aaron must cast lots for the two goats, one lot for the LORD and one for Azazel.
verses.tsw_comparator: Aaron shall cast lots over the two goats, one lot for the LORD and one lot for Azazel.

verses.rationale: Unfolds the lot going up upon the goat into natural selection language and retains the sacrificial designation.
verses.before: Aaron will bring forward the goat on which the lot for the LORD fell and prepare it as a sin offering.
verses.after: He must bring forward the goat chosen by the lot for the LORD and offer it as a sin offering.
verses.tsw_comparator: Aaron shall bring forward the goat on which the lot for the LORD fell and prepare it as a sin offering.

verses.rationale: Retains alive, both occurrences of Azazel, divine presence and the ambiguous atonement-over-it formulation rather than deciding between for it and by means of it.
verses.before: But the goat on which the lot for Azazel fell will be presented alive before the LORD to make atonement over it, so that it may be sent away into the wilderness for Azazel.
verses.after: But the goat chosen by the lot for Azazel must be kept alive before the LORD, to make atonement over it and send it away to Azazel in the wilderness.
verses.tsw_comparator: But the goat on which the lot for Azazel fell shall be presented alive before the LORD to make atonement over it, so that it may be sent away into the wilderness for Azazel.

verses.rationale: Keeps the deliberate resumption of verse 6 and the added slaughter action, repeating the bull's personal offering role.
verses.before: Aaron will bring forward the bull of the sin offering that is for himself, make atonement for himself and his household, and slaughter the bull of the sin offering that is for himself.
verses.after: Aaron must present the bull for his own sin offering and make atonement for himself and his household. He must slaughter the bull for his own sin offering.
verses.tsw_comparator: Aaron shall bring forward the bull of the sin offering that is for himself, make atonement for himself and his household, and slaughter the bull of the sin offering that is for himself.

verses.rationale: Preserves the full censer, two cupped handfuls, finely ground incense, altar source and movement into the inner room.
verses.before: He will take a firepan full of burning coals from the altar before the LORD and two handfuls of finely ground fragrant incense and bring them inside the curtain.
verses.after: He must take a censer full of burning coals from the altar before the LORD and two handfuls of finely ground fragrant incense, and bring them behind the curtain.
verses.tsw_comparator: He shall take a firepan full of burning coals from the altar before the LORD and two handfuls of finely ground fragrant incense and bring them inside the curtain.

verses.rationale: Retains the testimony rather than replacing it with ark, explains it selectively in vocabulary, and keeps the incense cloud's stated protective purpose.
verses.before: He will put the incense on the fire before the LORD, so that the cloud of incense covers the atonement cover that is over the testimony, and he will not die.
verses.after: There before the LORD, he must put the incense on the coals so that its cloud covers the atonement cover above the testimony. Then he will not die.
verses.tsw_comparator: He shall put the incense on the fire before the LORD, so that the cloud of incense covers the atonement cover that is over the testimony, and he will not die.

verses.rationale: Distinguishes blood on the east-facing side from seven sprinklings in front. The alternative eastward directional reading is noted, and no first-action count is invented.
verses.before: He will take some of the bull’s blood and sprinkle it with his finger on the east side of the atonement cover. Before the atonement cover he will sprinkle some of the blood with his finger seven times.
verses.after: He must take some of the bull's blood and sprinkle it with his finger on the east side of the atonement cover. Then he must sprinkle some of the blood with his finger seven times in front of the cover.
verses.tsw_comparator: He shall take some of the bull’s blood and sprinkle it with his finger on the east side of the atonement cover. Before the atonement cover he shall sprinkle some of the blood with his finger seven times.

verses.rationale: Preserves the people's goat versus Aaron's bull, repeated entry and both blood locations, without merging the two animal rites.
verses.before: Then he will slaughter the goat of the sin offering that is for the people and bring its blood inside the curtain. He will do with its blood as he did with the bull’s blood, sprinkling it on the atonement cover and before the atonement cover.
verses.after: He must slaughter the goat for the people's sin offering and bring its blood behind the curtain. He must do with its blood what he did with the bull's blood, sprinkling it on the atonement cover and in front of it.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then he shall slaughter the goat of the sin offering that is for the people and bring its blood inside the curtain. He shall do with its blood as he did with the bull’s blood, sprinkling it on the atonement cover and before the atonement cover.

verses.rationale: Retains sanctuary purification and the distinct impurity/rebellion/sin terms; preserves the tent dwelling among an impure people rather than only among the already clean.
verses.before: Thus he will make atonement for the Holy Place because of the uncleannesses of the Israelites and because of their transgressions, all their sins. He will do the same for the Tent of Meeting, which dwells with them among their uncleannesses.
verses.after: In this way he must make atonement for the inner sanctuary because of the Israelites' impurities and rebellions, all their sins. He must do the same for the tent of meeting, which stands among them in the midst of their impurities.
verses.tsw_comparator: Thus he shall make atonement for the Holy Place because of the uncleannesses of the Israelites and because of their transgressions, all their sins. He shall do the same for the Tent of Meeting, which dwells with them in the midst of their uncleannesses.

verses.rationale: Makes the necessary Aaron exception explicit and retains the complete interval and three groups for whom atonement is made.
verses.before: No one will be in the Tent of Meeting from the time he enters to make atonement in the Holy Place until he comes out and has made atonement for himself, for his household, and for the whole assembly of Israel.
verses.after: No one else may be in the tent of meeting from the time Aaron enters to make atonement in the inner sanctuary until he comes out. He must make atonement for himself, his household, and the whole assembly of Israel.
verses.tsw_comparator: No one shall be in the Tent of Meeting from the time he enters to make atonement in the Holy Place until he comes out and has made atonement for himself, for his household, and for the whole assembly of Israel.

verses.rationale: Retains movement outward, both blood sources and all altar horns; does not identify the unnamed altar or supply a mixing procedure.
verses.before: Then he will go out to the altar that is before the LORD and make atonement for it. He will take some of the bull’s blood and some of the goat’s blood and put it on the horns of the altar on all sides.
verses.after: Then he must go out to the altar before the LORD and make atonement for it. He must take some of the bull's blood and the goat's blood and put it on the horns all around the altar.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then he shall go out to the altar that is before the LORD and make atonement for it. He shall take some of the bull’s blood and some of the goat’s blood and put it on the horns of the altar on all sides.

verses.rationale: Preserves seven sprinklings plus both cleansing and consecration rather than treating these as interchangeable filler.
verses.before: He will sprinkle some of the blood on it with his finger seven times and cleanse it and make it holy from the uncleannesses of the Israelites.
verses.after: He must sprinkle some of the blood on it with his finger seven times, cleansing it from the Israelites' impurities and making it holy.
verses.tsw_comparator: He shall sprinkle some of the blood on it with his finger seven times and cleanse it and make it holy from the uncleannesses of the Israelites.

verses.rationale: Keeps all three completed sacred-space rites before the live goat's presentation.
verses.before: When Aaron has finished making atonement for the Holy Place, the Tent of Meeting, and the altar, he will bring forward the live goat.
verses.after: When he has finished making atonement for the inner sanctuary, the tent of meeting, and the altar, he must bring forward the live goat.
verses.tsw_comparator: When Aaron has finished making atonement for the Holy Place, the Tent of Meeting, and the altar, he shall bring forward the live goat.

verses.rationale: Preserves both hands, following the read plural alongside written hand, all three wrongdoing terms, transfer to the head and an appointed male escort; ready is an alternative for itti.
verses.before: Aaron will lay both his hands on the head of the live goat and confess over it all the iniquities of the Israelites and all their transgressions, all their sins. He will place them on the head of the goat and send it away into the wilderness by the hand of a person appointed for the task.
verses.after: Aaron must lay both hands on the live goat's head and confess over it all the Israelites' wrongdoing and all their rebellions, all their sins. He must place them on the goat's head and send it into the wilderness with a man appointed for the task.
verses.tsw_comparator: Aaron shall lay both his hands on the head of the live goat and confess over it all the iniquities of the Israelites and all their transgressions, all their sins. He shall place them on the head of the goat and send it away into the wilderness by the hand of a person appointed for the task.

verses.rationale: Keeps the concrete carrying image and wrongdoing term linked to verse 21; renders cut-off land as remote without adding a cliff or a killing.
verses.before: The goat will carry upon itself all their iniquities to a remote land, and the person will release the goat in the wilderness.
verses.after: The goat will carry all their wrongdoing on itself to a remote land. The man must release the goat in the wilderness.
verses.tsw_comparator: The goat shall carry upon itself all their iniquities to a remote land, and the person shall release the goat in the wilderness.

verses.rationale: Preserves reentry, the specified linen clothes, their earlier use and leaving them at the tent.
verses.before: Aaron will enter the Tent of Meeting, take off the linen garments he put on when he entered the Holy Place, and leave them there.
verses.after: Aaron must then enter the tent of meeting, take off the linen garments he wore when he entered the inner sanctuary, and leave them there.
verses.tsw_comparator: Aaron shall enter the Tent of Meeting, take off the linen garments he put on when he entered the Holy Place, and leave them there.

verses.rationale: Keeps the separate bathing, clothing change, two burnt offerings and their beneficiaries without adding household here from adjacent formulations.
verses.before: He will bathe his body in water in a holy place and put on his garments. Then he will come out and prepare his burnt offering and the people’s burnt offering, making atonement for himself and for the people.
verses.after: He must bathe his body in water in a holy place and put on his clothes. Then he must come out and offer his burnt offering and the people's burnt offering, making atonement for himself and for the people.
verses.tsw_comparator: He shall bathe his body in water in a holy place and put on his garments. Then he shall come out and prepare his burnt offering and the people’s burnt offering, making atonement for himself and for the people.

verses.rationale: Retains the short fat-burning instruction and altar destination; no whole-carcass burning is introduced here.
verses.before: He will turn the fat of the sin offering into smoke on the altar.
verses.after: He must burn the fat of the sin offering on the altar.
verses.tsw_comparator: He shall turn the fat of the sin offering into smoke on the altar.

verses.rationale: Keeps the escort's cleansing and subsequent return separate from Aaron's washing; retains the fourth occurrence of Azazel.
verses.before: The one who releases the goat for Azazel will wash his clothes and bathe his body in water, and afterward may come into the camp.
verses.after: The man who releases the goat for Azazel must wash his clothes and bathe his body in water. After that he may enter the camp.
verses.tsw_comparator: The one who releases the goat for Azazel shall wash his clothes and bathe his body in water, and afterward may come into the camp.

verses.rationale: Preserves both carcasses, the reason given by their blood's use, outside-camp disposal and all three materials; leaves the unnamed carrying/burning agents open.
verses.before: The bull of the sin offering and the goat of the sin offering, whose blood was brought into the Holy Place to make atonement, will be carried outside the camp, and their skins, flesh, and dung will be burned with fire.
verses.after: The bull and goat of the sin offerings, whose blood was brought into the inner sanctuary for atonement, must be taken outside the camp. Their hides, flesh, and dung must be burned in the fire.
verses.tsw_comparator: The bull of the sin offering and the goat of the sin offering, whose blood was brought into the Holy Place to make atonement, shall be carried outside the camp, and their skins, flesh, and dung shall be burned with fire.

verses.rationale: Retains the burner's separate cleansing and return, with generic participial referent rather than an added priestly identity.
verses.before: The one who burns them will wash his clothes and bathe his body in water, and afterward may come into the camp.
verses.after: The person who burns them must wash their clothes and bathe their body in water. After that they may enter the camp.
verses.tsw_comparator: The one who burns them shall wash his clothes and bathe his body in water, and afterward may come into the camp.

verses.rationale: Preserves exact date, self-affliction as enacted self-denial, all-work prohibition and equal native/sojourner scope; does not reduce the command to an inward attitude or specify only fasting.
verses.before: This will be a perpetual statute for you: in the seventh month, on the tenth day of the month, you will humble yourselves and do no work, whether the native-born or the resident alien who lives among you.
verses.after: This is a lasting statute for you. On the tenth day of the seventh month, you must deny yourselves and do no work. This applies to both the native-born and foreigners living among you.
verses.tsw_comparator: This shall be a perpetual statute for you: in the seventh month, on the tenth day of the month, you shall humble yourselves and do no work, whether the native-born or the resident alien who lives among you.

verses.rationale: Leaves the unstated atonement agent open and follows the Hebrew accent division attaching from all your sins to the final clean clause; the alternative attachment is noted.
verses.before: For on this day atonement will be made for you, to cleanse you; from all your sins you will be clean before the LORD.
verses.after: For on this day atonement will be made for you to cleanse you. You will be clean from all your sins before the LORD.
verses.tsw_comparator: For on this day atonement shall be made for you, to cleanse you; from all your sins you shall be clean before the LORD.

verses.rationale: Preserves intensified sabbath rest, repeated self-denial and repeated lasting status without reducing the instruction to a weekly date.
verses.before: It will be a Sabbath of complete rest for you, and you will humble yourselves. It is a perpetual statute.
verses.after: It is a sabbath of complete rest for you, and you must deny yourselves. This is a lasting statute.
verses.tsw_comparator: It shall be a Sabbath of complete rest for you, and you shall humble yourselves. It is a perpetual statute.

verses.rationale: Renders filling the hand as ordination, retains father-son succession and the repeated holiness of the linen garments, continuing into verse 33.
verses.before: The priest who is anointed and whose hand is filled to serve as priest in his father’s place will make atonement. He will put on the linen garments, the holy garments,
verses.after: The priest anointed and ordained to serve in his father's place must make atonement. He must put on the linen garments, the holy garments,
verses.tsw_comparator: The priest who is anointed and whose hand is filled to serve as priest in his father’s place shall make atonement. He shall put on the linen garments, the holy garments,

verses.rationale: Keeps the inner sanctuary distinct and all five objects or beneficiaries of atonement, preserving the repeated verb without replacing cleansing of places with forgiveness.
verses.before: and make atonement for the holy sanctuary, the Tent of Meeting, and the altar; he will make atonement for the priests and for all the people of the assembly.
verses.after: and make atonement for the inner sanctuary. He must make atonement for the tent of meeting and the altar, and for the priests and all the assembled people.
verses.tsw_comparator: and make atonement for the holy sanctuary, the Tent of Meeting, and the altar; he shall make atonement for the priests and for all the people of the assembly.

verses.rationale: Retains once a year, all sins and the narrative past-tense completion; identifies the implicit he as Aaron and records alternatives without inventing a date of performance.
verses.before: This will be a perpetual statute for you, to make atonement for the Israelites because of all their sins once each year.” And it was done as the LORD commanded Moses.
verses.after: This is a lasting statute for you: atonement must be made for the Israelites once a year for all their sins.” Aaron did as the LORD had commanded Moses.
verses.tsw_comparator: This shall be a perpetual statute for you, to make atonement for the Israelites because of all their sins once each year.” And it was done as the LORD commanded Moses.

verses.rationale: Keeps Moses as the sole direct recipient, followed by the wider instructed audience.
verses.before: The LORD spoke to Moses, saying,
verses.after: The LORD spoke to Moses:
verses.tsw_comparator: The LORD spoke to Moses, saying,

verses.rationale: Preserves priestly and community audiences and the command formula; colon permits the quoted message to run naturally into verse 3.
verses.before: “Speak to Aaron and his sons and to all the Israelites, and say to them: This is what the LORD has commanded.
verses.after: “Speak to Aaron, his sons, and all the Israelites. Tell them: This is what the LORD has commanded:
verses.tsw_comparator: “Speak to Aaron and his sons and to all the Israelites, and say to them: This is what the LORD has commanded.

verses.rationale: Retains all three domestic species and both locations. The general slaughter rule is not silently restricted to already intended sacrifices; the conditional sentence continues in verse 4.
verses.before: If someone from the house of Israel slaughters an ox, lamb, or goat in the camp or slaughters it outside the camp,
verses.after: If anyone of the house of Israel slaughters an ox, a sheep, or a goat, either inside or outside the camp,
verses.tsw_comparator: If anyone from the house of Israel slaughters an ox, lamb, or goat in the camp or slaughters it outside the camp,

verses.rationale: Keeps blood reckoned as guilt, repeated shedding and the severe but unspecified cut-off penalty; preserves tent entrance and divine ownership of the tabernacle.
verses.before: and does not bring it to the entrance of the Tent of Meeting to present it as an offering to the LORD before the LORD’s tabernacle, bloodguilt will be reckoned to that person. Blood has been shed, and that person will be cut off from among the people.
verses.after: but does not bring it to the entrance to the tent of meeting to present it as an offering to the LORD before his tabernacle, that person is guilty of bloodshed. They have shed blood and must be cut off from their people.
verses.tsw_comparator: and does not bring it to the entrance of the Tent of Meeting to present it as an offering to the LORD before the LORD’s tabernacle, bloodguilt shall be reckoned to that person. Blood has been shed, and that person shall be cut off from among the people.

verses.rationale: Retains the explicit purpose, repeated bringing, country versus tent location, priest and peace-offering classification.
verses.before: This is so that the Israelites may bring the sacrifices they are sacrificing in the open field and bring them to the LORD at the entrance of the Tent of Meeting, to the priest, and sacrifice them as sacrifices of well-being to the LORD.
verses.after: This is so the Israelites will bring the sacrifices they offer in the open country to the LORD, to the priest at the entrance to the tent of meeting, and offer them there as peace offerings to the LORD.
verses.tsw_comparator: This is so that the Israelites may bring the sacrifices they are sacrificing in the open field and bring them to the LORD at the entrance of the Tent of Meeting, to the priest, and sacrifice them as sacrifices of well-being to the LORD.

verses.rationale: Preserves splashing rather than sprinkling, fat, aroma and location; does not add all around from other verses or versions.
verses.before: The priest will dash the blood against the LORD’s altar at the entrance of the Tent of Meeting and turn the fat into smoke as a pleasing aroma to the LORD.
verses.after: The priest must splash the blood against the LORD's altar at the entrance to the tent of meeting and burn the fat as a pleasing aroma to the LORD.
verses.tsw_comparator: The priest shall dash the blood against the LORD’s altar at the entrance of the Tent of Meeting and turn the fat into smoke as a pleasing aroma to the LORD.

verses.rationale: Retains seirim as goat demons in the cultic context and the source's sexual metaphor for allegiance, not merely generic unfaithfulness; no equation with Azazel is asserted.
verses.before: They will no longer sacrifice their sacrifices to goat-demons, after whom they prostitute themselves. This will be a perpetual statute for them throughout their generations.
verses.after: They must no longer offer their sacrifices to goat demons, prostituting themselves by going after them. This is a lasting statute for them throughout their generations.
verses.tsw_comparator: They shall no longer sacrifice their sacrifices to goat-demons, after whom they prostitute themselves. This shall be a perpetual statute for them throughout their generations.

verses.rationale: Preserves explicit inclusion of the resident foreigner at this new rule and both offering categories; retains their rather than silently changing the source pronoun to your.
verses.before: You will say to them: If someone from the house of Israel or from the resident aliens who live among them presents a burnt offering or sacrifice,
verses.after: Tell them also: If anyone of the house of Israel, or any foreigner living among them, offers a burnt offering or a sacrifice,
verses.tsw_comparator: You shall say to them: If anyone from the house of Israel or from the resident aliens who live among them presents a burnt offering or sacrifice,

verses.rationale: Keeps the precise presentation requirement and the repeated cut-off penalty rather than paraphrasing it as a lighter exclusion.
verses.before: and does not bring it to the entrance of the Tent of Meeting to prepare it for the LORD, that person will be cut off from the people.
verses.after: but does not bring it to the entrance to the tent of meeting to offer it to the LORD, that person must be cut off from their people.
verses.tsw_comparator: and does not bring it to the entrance of the Tent of Meeting to prepare it for the LORD, that person shall be cut off from the people.

verses.rationale: Retains the face image, any blood, both populations and God's explicit agency, which the passive penalties elsewhere do not specify.
verses.before: If someone from the house of Israel or from the resident aliens who live among them eats any blood, I will set my face against the person who eats the blood and cut that person off from among the people.
verses.after: If anyone of the house of Israel, or any foreigner living among them, eats any blood, I will set my face against that person who eats blood and cut them off from their people.
verses.tsw_comparator: If anyone from the house of Israel or from the resident aliens who live among them eats any blood, I will set my face against the person who eats the blood and cut that person off from among the people.

verses.rationale: Preserves flesh, life, God's emphatic gift and your lives; takes be-nefesh instrumentally and explains the alternate price/exchange reading without importing a theory of atonement.
verses.before: For the life of the flesh is in the blood, and I have given it to you upon the altar to make atonement for your lives, for the blood makes atonement by means of the life.
verses.after: For the life of the flesh is in the blood, and I myself have given it to you on the altar to make atonement for your lives. It is the blood that makes atonement through the life it carries.
verses.tsw_comparator: For the life of the flesh is in the blood, and I have given it to you upon the altar to make atonement for your lives, for the blood makes atonement by means of the life.

verses.rationale: Retains the repeated prohibition for Israelites and resident foreigners and marks the recalled direct instruction clearly.
verses.before: So I have said to the Israelites: No one among you will eat blood, and no resident alien living among you will eat blood.
verses.after: That is why I have told the Israelites, ‘None of you may eat blood, and no foreigner living among you may eat blood.’
verses.tsw_comparator: Therefore I have said to the Israelites: No one among you shall eat blood, and no resident alien living among you shall eat blood.

verses.rationale: Keeps edible wild game distinct from the three domestic species, with both pouring out and covering required; preserves both populations.
verses.before: If someone from the Israelites or from the resident aliens who live among them hunts an animal or bird that may be eaten, the person will pour out its blood and cover it with dust.
verses.after: If any Israelite or any foreigner living among them hunts a wild animal or bird that may be eaten, they must pour out its blood and cover it with earth.
verses.tsw_comparator: If anyone from the Israelites or from the resident aliens who live among them hunts an animal or bird that may be eaten, the person shall pour out its blood and cover it with dust.

verses.rationale: Retains the difficult first clause's repeated life term and the repeated blood/life explanation, followed by universal prohibition and penalty; flesh is rendered creature in the distributive phrase.
verses.before: For the life of every flesh is its blood; its blood is its life. Therefore I said to the Israelites: You will not eat the blood of any flesh, for the life of every flesh is its blood. Whoever eats it will be cut off.
verses.after: For the life of every creature is its blood, which carries its life. So I have told the Israelites, ‘You must not eat the blood of any creature, because the life of every creature is its blood. Anyone who eats it must be cut off.’
verses.tsw_comparator: For the life of every flesh is its blood; its blood is its life. Therefore I said to the Israelites: You shall not eat the blood of any flesh, for the life of every flesh is its blood. Whoever eats it shall be cut off.

verses.rationale: Preserves both kinds of carcass, both populations and the full washing/bathing/evening sequence; does not turn the stated consequence into an affirmative permission to eat carrion.
verses.before: Anyone, whether native-born or resident alien, who eats an animal that died by itself or was torn by animals will wash their clothes, bathe in water, and be unclean until evening; then that person will be clean.
verses.after: Anyone, whether native-born or a foreigner, who eats an animal that died on its own or was torn by wild animals must wash their clothes and bathe in water. They remain unclean until evening; then they will be clean.
verses.tsw_comparator: Anyone, whether native-born or resident alien, who eats an animal that died by itself or was torn by animals shall wash their clothes, bathe in water, and be unclean until evening; then that person shall be clean.

verses.rationale: Retains the source's and between the failures and the bear-guilt idiom, with responsibility for consequences explained; no penalty mechanism is invented.
verses.before: But if the person does not wash the clothes and bathe the body, that person will bear guilt.”
verses.after: But if they do not wash their clothes and do not bathe their body, they must bear their guilt.”
verses.tsw_comparator: But if the person does not wash the clothes and bathe the body, that person shall bear guilt.”
